report.source_text: On physical examination, the area of itching skin was grossly normal. Neurologic examination was notable for a positive Spurling sign bilaterally. He had 5/5 strength in the major myotomes of the upper extremities and a 2+ bicep and triceps reflex response on a symmetric fashion. He denied decreased sensation in the distal dermatomes.

report.source_text: The patient's chronic axial mechanical neck pain and bilateral upper extremity radiculopathy correlated with the degenerative and stenotic segments from C3 through C7. The pruritus was possibly caused by compression of the nerve roots and/or spinal cord at the affected levels. Given his multiyear history of multimodal conservative therapies and correlation between imaging and physical examination, it was thought that surgical intervention in the form of an ACDF from C3 to C7 would provide the patient permanent relief of his pain and pruritus.

report.source_text: After surgery, the patient's symptoms improved instantly. At his most recent visit four months postoperatively, the patient related 95% improvement in his preoperative symptoms without any notable pain and only occasional sensation of pruritus.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 56-year-old male presented with chronic disabling bilateral upper extremity pruritus and neck pain involving C6 dermatomal distribution. Prior multidisciplinary evaluation excluded dermatologic and peripheral neuropathic causes. Cervical spine MRI revealed multilevel cervical spondylosis, spinal stenosis at C3-4 and C4-5, and multilevel foraminal stenosis from C3 to C7 consistent with radiculopathy. Physical examination showed positive bilateral Spurling sign without motor deficits or sensory loss. Despite absence of electrodiagnostic confirmation, imaging and clinical correlation supported neuropathic pruritus due to nerve root/spinal cord compression. Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) from C3 to C7 was performed without complication. Postoperatively, the patient reported immediate and sustained 95% symptom improvement at four months, confirming neuropathic etiology consistent with BRP.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Multilevel cervical spondylosis and severe foraminal stenosis from C3 to C7 causing nerve root/spinal cord compression
Clinical features including bilateral disabling pruritus in a C6 dermatome distribution, positive Spurling sign, and normal strength/reflexes without sensory loss
Surgical ACDF from C3 to C7 planned due to correlation of symptoms and imaging findings
Postoperative rapid and sustained 95% improvement of pruritus and pain symptoms at four months
